items.author: joshuaswarren
items.body:
## omp / Oh My Pi companion (soft offer)

Hi — thank you for [Unlazy](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy). We are using the skill + `gate-check.mjs` heavily.

Claude Code’s Stop hook does not run inside **omp (Oh My Pi)** / herdr live panes, so we published a small companion extension that only adds omp lifecycle hooks and slash commands, still shelling out to your upstream `gate-check.mjs` (no reimplementation of CHECK/EXPECT):

**https://github.com/joshuaswarren/omp-unlazy-guard**

README credits Unlazy prominently. MIT.

This is a soft offer, not a request to merge our code into your tree.
items.title: Companion: omp/pi Unlazy guard extension (soft offer)

## Summary

Unlazy can correctly execute, reverify, and Stop-enforce every gate that exists while the gate set itself omits part of the requested work.

The exact demonstrated shape is:

```text
original request requires deliverable A and deliverable B
→ PLAN/tree/ledger contains A only
→ A's gate observes A and passes honestly
→ every declared gate is met
→ parent/status/Stop see no unmet gate
→ the task can be reported complete although B was never assigned or checked
```

items.title: UL003 — a multi-deliverable `PLAN` can omit required work while every declared gate passes

## Summary

Current Unlazy binds approval to the declared execution envelope of a gate: ledger and gate identity, exact `CHECK:` and `EXPECT:`, resolved working directory and shell, timeout, output and regex limits, platform, and inherited `PATH`. That is a strong consent boundary for the command text the user reviewed.

It does not bind two different kinds of file identity that can matter after approval or after a green result:

1. **oracle identity** — repository-hosted script or checker bytes invoked by an unchanged `CHECK:`; and
2. **input identity** — target or input bytes that the succes
items.title: UL002 — gate approval and evidence can remain current after the checked script or input changes

items.author: theislampill
items.body:
## Summary

Unlazy already describes abandonment correctly: an impossible required gate may remain in the ledger with `ABANDON: <id> <reason>`, and that state is a visible handoff rather than verified completion. Current runtime behavior does not preserve that distinction.

On current `main` (`754d9a68109e39b836cc72a39fb9a823f9d6b613`, tree `80e432e3228f126061b8a1f34d85c9167c569bf9`), a ledger whose remaining required gate is abandoned prints `ALL MET (...)` and exits `0`. The stock parent integration gate re-runs children and expects `ALL MET`, so the same abandoned child can satisfy parent v
items.title: UL001 — abandoned required gates can still receive `ALL MET` and parent completion credit

items.author: H5H-Stoven-One
items.body:
## Summary

`gate-check.mjs <file>` silently ignores the file argument when `--timeout` is not passed. It falls back to scanning the current working directory instead. This is the exact invocation form the SKILL.md documents.

## Cause

`scripts/gate-check.mjs`:

```js
const tIdx = args.indexOf("--timeout");
const fileArgs = args.filter((a, i) => !a.startsWith("--") && i !== tIdx + 1);
```

When `--timeout` is absent, `indexOf` returns `-1`, so `tIdx + 1` is `0`. The filter then drops whatever sits at index 0 — the first positional argument.

```
["GATES.md"]                  tIdx=-1  -> files
items.title: gate-check.mjs silently ignores its file argument unless --timeout is passed

items.author: silvereyes137-eng
items.body:
On Windows, whether a gate passes depends on which shell launched `gate-check.mjs`, not on
the state of the work. The same gate file and the same checker produce opposite verdicts.

CONTRIBUTING rule 6 says scripts stay "Node 16+ standard library only, Windows and POSIX
both", so filing this as a bug rather than a portability wish.

**Environment:** Windows 11, Node 24.18.0, unlazy at `ed9e8d2`, unmodified.

## Reproduction

`GATES.md`, with a check in the style the README itself uses:

```
# Gates: shell portability

- [ ] S1: a POSIX pipeline check
  CHECK: echo hello world | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z'
items.title: gate-check: the same gate passes or fails depending on which shell launched it (Windows)
